title: Artificial Intelligence-driven Assessment of Sleep Quality: Comparing Artificial Intelligence-generated Sleep Questionnaire with Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index in Undergraduate Medical Students
journal: Global Journal of Medical, Pharmaceutical, and Biomedical Update

sections.abstract: <jats:sec id="st1"> <jats:title>Objectives:</jats:title> <jats:p>Recently, artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly utilized in sleep medicine for various tasks, including scoring respiratory events and staging sleep. Regardless of these AI developments in the field of sleep, sleep assessment devices require stringent validation to enhance the reliability and accuracy of their reports. The present study aims to analyze the performance of an AI-generated assessment tool of sleep quality in comparison with the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) among undergraduate medical students. By evaluating this agreement and comparing these two assessment tools, we aim to explore the potential of AI in expanding personalized sleep medicine.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec id="st2"> <jats:title>Material and Methods:</jats:title> <jats:p>This was a cross-sectional study conducted among 300 undergraduate medical students using two sleep assessment tools. The first is the traditional PSQI tool, and the second is an AI-generated sleep quality assessment tool for undergraduate medical students, structured and designed by Chat-GPT, which utilizes the same seven domains as the PSQI.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec id="st3"> <jats:title>Results:</jats:title> <jats:p>The current study found out that the mean score of the AI-generated assessment (10.65 ± 2.30) was lower than the mean PSQI score (11.94 ± 2.45). In addition, a slight agreement was found between these two scores, which was shown by Cohen’s weighted kappa coefficient of 0.133. This suggests that the AI tool may underestimate the sleep quality assessment compared to PSQI scoring.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec id="st4"> <jats:title>Conclusion:</jats:title> <jats:p>While the AI-generated questionnaire for sleep quality assessment has the potential benefit of scalability and automation in research, the present study highlights the crucial necessity for careful training and validation of AI tools.</jats:p> </jats:sec>
